findings.claim: The new failure-code/layer invariant is fail-open on drift: the table is typed `Map<string, string>` and an unmapped code silently skips the check, so a failure code added to `PROMPT_REFINER_FAILURE_CODES` but omitted from the table accepts any `failureLayer`, which is exactly the combination criterion 5 asks the strict schema to validate.
findings.reproduction: Add `"budget_exhausted"` to `PROMPT_REFINER_FAILURE_CODES` (lib/promptRefinerReceiptCore.ts:35) and to `PRE_DISPATCH_ONLY_FAILURE_CODES` (:49), leaving `FAILURE_LAYER_BY_CODE` unchanged. `npm run typecheck` still passes, and `promptRefinerExecutionReceiptSchema.safeParse(execution({ outcome: "refused_before_dispatch", suggestionId: null, provider: null, modelId: null, adapterVersion: null, dispatchedAt: null, completedAt: "2026-09-15T00:00:00.050Z", preparationLatencyMs: 50, inputTokens: null, cachedInputTokens: null, outputTokens: null, reasoningTokens: null, actualCostMicroUsd: null, failureCode: "budget_exhausted", failureLayer: "adapter" }))` returns `success: true`; expected `false`. Typing the table as `Record<Exclude<FailureCode, "cancelled">, FailureLayer>` and treating an unmapped code as an issue makes the omission a compile error instead.

findings.claim: `as const satisfies readonly PromptRefinerTerminalReason[]` only checks that each listed element is a valid reason, not that every reason is listed, so the exported list and the bijection test can silently miss a reason even though the switch is exhaustiveness-checked.
findings.reproduction: Add `| "provider_refused"` to the `PromptRefinerTerminalReason` union (:385) and a matching `case` in `promptRefinerTerminalReceiptFacts` (:455) without touching the array. `npm run typecheck` passes and `tests/promptRefinerExecutionContract.test.mjs` still passes, yet `PROMPT_REFINER_TERMINAL_REASONS` omits the new reason. A coverage assertion such as `const _cover: Record<PromptRefinerTerminalReason, true>` built from the array would fail instead.

findings.claim: The failure-code union here hand-duplicates `PROMPT_REFINER_FAILURE_CODES` in lib/promptRefinerReceiptCore.ts with no type-level link, so the two can diverge without a compile error even though the mapping is the thing that must agree with the receipt schema.
findings.reproduction: Delete `"no_change"` from `PROMPT_REFINER_FAILURE_CODES` (lib/promptRefinerReceiptCore.ts:35). `npm run typecheck` reports no error in lib/promptRefinerExecutionContract.ts; only the runtime test fails. Deriving the union from the receipt-core `const` array (e.g. `(typeof PROMPT_REFINER_FAILURE_CODES)[number]`) turns the divergence into a typecheck failure.
